ditto_mark_csv_representation: Cells that contain a ditto mark in the scan are written as the literal character " in the CSV (CSV-escaped as """"). Resolving them to the repeated value is the parser's job, not the ground truth.
notes: Form headers and labels are in French; species names are written in German by the bander.
Page 1 has 8 blank rows at the top of the table (no bague number assigned), preserved in the CSV as empty rows so row positions match the scan.

Bague numbers are recorded as a 5-digit number where the leading '9' is printed on the form and the bander fills in the last 4 digits. We expanded these to full 5-digit numbers (e.g. '359' on the form -> '90359').
Sex column uses symbols: X = the cross/check mark used on the form, m = male (Mars symbol), f = female (Venus symbol). Parentheses like '(f)' indicate uncertain sex determination by the bander.
Ditto marks (", '', //, ii) are kept as the literal character " in the CSV - they are NOT resolved to the repeated species name. The parser/pipeline is expected to resolve them.
Foreign-ring recaptures appear in the notes column (e.g. 'Paris 1429551', 'Paris 12706261', '25009', '25010', '26700').
'Brutfleck' (brood patch) in the notes column marks breeding females.
Weights (Poids) are in grams; wing lengths (Aile) are in mm.

Handwriting quality degrades on pages 5-6; ambiguous cells are left as best-guess. Row 90519 ('Riley Ventoux') is an annotation in the species field rather than a bird entry; left without measurements.
